productDetailRestorations.original_cell: Frequently-bought, relatively low-priced (cigarettes, pens, groceries, batteries, newspapers). 3 sub-types: **staples** (bought regularly — bread, soap); **impulse products** (bought with little planning — chocolate, magazines); **emergency products** (bought under urgent need — umbrellas in a rainstorm).
productDetailRestorations.replacement_cell: Frequently-bought, relatively low-priced products. Source examples: cigarettes, pens, pencils, candies, groceries, flashlights batteries, sundry drugs, chewing gums, newspapers and flimsy shopping bags. Three sub-types: **staples** are products bought regularly, such as bread, bath soap, beverages and tooth paste; **impulse products** are purchased with little planning or search effort, such as chocolate and magazines; **emergency products** are purchased when the consumer’s need is urgent, such as umbrellas during a rainstorm.

productDetailRestorations.original_cell: Consumers compare price/quality/features across brands before buying — furniture, shoes, clothing, durables (fans, radios, TVs).
productDetailRestorations.replacement_cell: Consumers usually compare prices, quality and features of alternative brands before purchasing. Source examples: household furniture, shoes, clothing and consumer durables such as fans, radios, television sets and tape recorders.

productDetailRestorations.original_cell: Unprocessed goods used to produce other goods — farm products (wheat, cotton, livestock) and natural products (fish, lumber, crude petroleum, iron ore).
productDetailRestorations.replacement_cell: Unprocessed industrial goods used to produce other goods. Farm products include wheat, cotton, livestock, fruits and vegetables; natural products include fish, lumber, crude petroleum and iron ore.

productDetailRestorations.original_cell: Aid production but don't significantly affect production scale, and don't form part of the final product, but cost less than installations — office equipment, portable tree-cutting machines, forklifts, hand tools.
productDetailRestorations.replacement_cell: Industrial products used to aid an organisation’s production operations without any significant effect on its scale of production. Like installations, accessories do not form part of the final product, but they cost less than installations. Examples include office equipment such as computers and typewriters, portable tree-cutting machines, forklift trucks and factory hand tools.

productDetailRestorations.original_cell: Depleted during production, not part of the finished product — consumables (paper, ink, toner, stationery), maintenance/repair services, business advisory services.
productDetailRestorations.replacement_cell: Do not become part of the finished product but are depleted during production. These include business/office consumables — paper, ink, marker, toner and stationery — plus maintenance and repair services such as window cleaning and computer repair, and business advisory services such as legal services, management consulting and advertising. Such services are usually supplied under contract.
